body:
Rereview: independently assessed the revised V7 allocation in the complete current plan. V7 now directly requires both full-module commands after M2 changes and before milestone closeout, explicitly covering surrounding tests affected by shared fixtures/helpers. This removes dependence on interpreting M1 V2 execution as sufficient post-maintenance proof. The unchanged-audit reuse allowance remains bounded by RC-SR-15; a result predating a relevant helper/fixture change is expressly insufficient. No test target, consumer allocation, governing model, milestone dependency or final-review obligation changed. The complete sequencing/proof conclusions below remain justified, and no new material finding emerged.

Scope: isolated formal Delivery Review of the one registered primary plan, docs/plans/2026-09-08-design-derived-test-model.md. Current approved Design Review binds Test including the TEST-SR-03 diagnostic clarification and unchanged Workflow; the approved proposal remains applicable. The assessment covers sequencing and verification together, not implementation or deletion approval.

Traceability and allocation: pass. Every TEST-SR-01–13, changed WF-SR-17/Composition-path outcome, all eight Test boundary rows and all three named combined hazards are allocated to TG-01–04 and TG-FINAL-01. M1 makes the criterion/consumer/resource package coherent before M2 relies on it. TG-01 includes the eight representative applications, useful diagnostic-only case and renamed-duplicate counterexample; it also covers flaky sole protection plus missing authority, randomized environment limits, quarantine limits and unchanged RC judgment authority. TG-02 uses deterministic parity/structure plus explicit published-text and resource-loading inspection. Those semantic assessments are not misrepresented as keyword validation.

Sequence and scope: pass. M1 includes governance, eleven named quality consumers, eight maintenance consumers, exact shared sources, mapped boundary/specialist resources, assets and existing build/validation/candidate-metadata surfaces. I expanded the closed existing brace families and confirmed they resolve. Unlisted transitive resources may be inspected but require reviewed allocation before a necessary edit; policy conflicts return to Design and no required consumer may be silently deferred. Changes to generation helpers require demonstrated mechanical need. Canonical source ownership, public privacy and historical release preservation are explicit. Internal Test/RC/WF identifiers and contributor paths are excluded from shipped guidance, while internal governance retains traceability.

Bounded maintenance and proof: pass. Direct source and AST inspection confirm all 8 BuildSkillsTests and 10 ModelRecordTests methods named by the plan. Their loops/subtests contain distinct unknown-value, malformed table, non-applicability, path/symlink, fenced/indented authority and public read-only partitions; the plan includes every partition rather than treating method count as coverage. Build tests distinguish generation/resource parity, explicit/default output paths, helper validation and command-level error reporting. TG-03 requires actual obligation/oracle/violation/boundary/diagnostic analysis; TG-04 compares discovered cases and accounted partitions before/after and runs surrounding modules. Consolidation is only a candidate. Replacement detection precedes removal, uncertainty preserves tests, and a justified no-deletion audit is a legitimate complete outcome without inventing changes. Required unknown-value, public-path, compatibility and side-effect protection cannot be traded for smaller counts or green output.

Feasibility and commands: pass. Existing unittest entrypoints accept the V6 class selections and verbosity arguments. Adapter build/validation help confirms the V3 version/output-dir/adapter-root interface. Existing repository-owned scripts supply canonical, generator, package, model and complete-set checks; current candidate metadata regeneration is ordered before compatibility tests. No runtime/schema change is allocated. M2 V6 supplies scoped baseline/post-maintenance execution and revised V7 directly supplies both complete modules after changes, including shared-helper impact. Failed results retain correction/blocker ownership; overlapping shared-fixture suite invocations are explicitly prohibited. These are feasible planned commands, not claims that their eventual changed subjects already pass.

A read-only python scripts/select-validation.py --mode local probe currently reports untracked-authoritative-artifacts for the new Test model, proposal and plan. This is the existing tracked-basis prerequisite before final broad validation, resolved through ordinary authorized staging of those documents; it is not a policy or scope defect requiring a plan redesign. No local integrated pass is claimed. V10 must actually run with the final authoritative artifacts tracked, and PR mode, if separately authorized, must use full actual revisions. The plan preserves fresh changed-proof/current-state obligations and permits only affirmative unaffected-pass reuse under RC policy.

Recovery and final coherence: pass. Revert coherent guidance/package changes on failed adoption; restore lost test protection and preserve contradictory evidence; missing intended behavior returns to Design. Historical contracts, records and external permissions remain separately owned. M1/M2 each require independent review and corrections. The explicit lifecycle-closeout checkpoint requires a fresh independent complete-diff/cross-milestone assessment after both milestones even if M2 keeps every test, followed by distinct Verify. TG-FINAL-01 compares packaged criteria with actual maintenance claims and evidence; it cannot be substituted by milestone approval or a test-group exemption.

Evidence basis: read the complete primary plan, exact approved model/review basis, current proposal constraints, selected test classes and relevant command/source surfaces; mechanically inspected all relied-on identities. Author plan evidence supports readability/link/count checks only. Delivery Review does not preaudit or classify test deletions, execute implementation validation, initialize planned work, settle routing, or authorize PR/push/publication. No required correction, unresolved necessary decision or material allocation gap was identified. Return control at the isolated review boundary.
independence_basis: Independent delegated reviewer /root/independent_proposal_review did not author or edit the plan, Design, tests or consumer implementation. codex-author authored delivery allocation. Earlier involvement was independent proposal/Design assessment only. This execution read the full plan and inspected approved basis and concrete test/command surfaces independently, and writes review evidence only.
